issues.legal_issue: A tank that had already vested in the State under an earlier abolition law could not vest again under a later law providing for vesting of tanks not already vested.
material_facts: The tank had been recorded as vested in the State when the earlier abolition law came into force.
The tank was later settled with a person under a provision concerning tanks whose beds were under cultivation.
Authorities subsequently declared that the tank vested absolutely in the State under a later law.
issues.conclusion: The tank had already vested in the State under the earlier law, so it could not vest again under the later law.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 3 and 4 of the Madhya Pradesh Abolition of Proprietary Rights Act, proprietary rights and the specified property vested in the State. Section 5(g), which provided for settlement of certain tanks and their underlying land, did not mean that such a tank had not vested in the State. Section 251(1) of the Madhya Pradesh Land Revenue Code applied only to tanks not already vested in the State, as its express wording made clear. No earlier case was relied on.

predicates.appeal_concerning_later_tank_vesting: The proceeding is an appeal concerning a declaration that a tank vested in the State under a later vesting law.
predicates.tank_already_vested_in_state: The tank had already vested in the State under an earlier law before the later vesting law was applied.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns a later vesting declaration and the tank had already vested in the State, the tank cannot vest again under the later law.

issues.legal_issue: A factual finding that an interested person was not given a proper opportunity to be heard is not displaced on appeal without a basis for rejecting that finding.
material_facts: The High Court found that the interested person had not been afforded a proper opportunity to be heard in the administrative inquiry.
The Supreme Court found no ground for rejecting the High Court's factual conclusion.
issues.conclusion: The finding that a proper opportunity had not been afforded was accepted as final and binding.
issues.legal_principle: Section 251 of the Madhya Pradesh Land Revenue Code required notice to interested parties and an opportunity for them to be heard. The Supreme Court treated the High Court's conclusion on whether that opportunity had been afforded as a finding of fact and accepted it as final and binding because no ground had been shown for rejecting it. No earlier case was relied on.

predicates.appeal_from_factual_finding: The proceeding is an appeal in which a lower court has made a factual finding about whether a person received a proper opportunity to be heard.
predicates.lower_court_found_no_hearing_opportunity: The lower court found that an interested person was not given a proper opportunity to be heard in an inquiry.
predicates.no_basis_to_displace_finding: The appellant has shown no basis for rejecting the lower court's factual finding.

issues.definition: In an appeal, a lower court's finding that an interested person lacked a proper hearing opportunity remains binding when no basis for displacing it is shown.
